brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A flat, spear-shaped green tea from Huaining county in Anhui, with national geographical indication status. It grows around Shuangjian Mountain near Longchi Hermitage, at about 400 metres, in misty country.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: The name is said to come from its high-mountain aroma and emerald colour. It is regarded as a choice green tea of Huaining; little more is documented about its past.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Flat and spear-like, with sturdy buds and leaves, glossy green and downy.
appearance_wet: Sturdy, tender buds and leaves of a bright green.
taste_profile: Fresh and mellow with a sweet return and a clean, lasting aroma.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
